translations.text: Paul, servant of God and apostle of Christ Jesus, according to the faith of God's elect and by the knowledge of the truth that belongs to the service of God,
by the hope of eternal life, which the God who does not lie promised before eternal times,
but in his own times he revealed his word through the preaching with which I was entrusted by the command of God our Savior,
to Titus, true son according to our common faith: grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you might set in order what is lacking and appoint elders in city after city, as I commanded you:
whoever is blameless, the husband of one wife, let him have believing children who are not accused of debauchery or disobedience.
For a bishop must be spotless, as a steward of God: not self-willed, not hot-tempered, not given to wine, not a brawler, not a seeker of shameful gain,
but a lover of guests, a lover of what is good, pure, righteous, worthy, patient, holding fast in accordance with the teaching of
the word of faith, so that he may be able both to give comfort in the teaching of life and to refute those who answer back.
For there are many who are insubordinate, speakers of vanity and deceivers of the mind, especially those of the circumcision,
whose mouths must be stopped, who overturn entire households, teaching what ought not to be taught for the sake of shameful gain.
One of them, their own prophet, said: "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies."
This testimony is true. Therefore reprove them unsparingly, so that they may be alive in faith,
and let them not heed Jewish fables and the commandment of men who have turned away from the truth.
For all things are pure to the pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure, but both their heart and their mind are defiled.
They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny him; they are detestable and disobedient and unproven for every good work.
But you, speak what befits the teaching of life:
Let the elders be vigilant, worthy, pure, alive in faith, in love, in patience;
the aged women likewise beautiful in composure, not slanderers, not subject to much wine, teachers of what is good,
so that they may instruct the young women to be lovers of their husbands, lovers of their children,
pure, spotless, keepers of the house, good, submissive to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be blasphemed.
Likewise exhort the young men to be pure.
In all things offer yourself as an example of good works, in your teaching showing incorruption, dignity, integrity,
a living, irreproachable word, so that the opponent may be ashamed and have nothing evil to say against us.
Let slaves submit to their own masters and be pleasing in everything, not answering back.
Let them not be pilferers, but let them show all good faith, so that they may adorn the teaching of our Savior God in all things.
For the grace of God has appeared as Savior to all people,
to instruct us, so that we may renounce ungodliness and worldly desire, and live in holiness and righteousness and godliness in this world,
and await that blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for us, so that he might redeem us from all lawlessness and purify for himself a people acquired as his own, imitators of good works.
Speak these things, and exhort and reprove with all authority; let no one despise you.
Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities and to be obedient, and to be prepared for every good work,
to blaspheme no one, to be free of contention, kind, showing all gentleness toward all people.
For we too were once ignorant and disobedient, led astray, and we served many desires and pleasures; we lived in wickedness and envy, hurtful and hating one another.
But when the sweetness and love for humankind of our Savior God appeared,
not from works of righteousness that we had done, but by his mercy he saved us, through the washing of rebirth and the renewal of the Holy Spirit,
which he poured out upon us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that we may be justified by his grace and become heirs of the hope of eternal life.
The saying is trustworthy; and I want you to affirm these things firmly, so that those who believe in God may take care to persevere in good works; for this is good and profitable for people.
But keep away from foolish inquiries and genealogies and quarrels and disputes about the law, for they are unprofitable and vain.
Keep away from a heretical man after one or two instructions.
Know that such a person is perverted and sins, and is self-condemned.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, hurry to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have chosen to spend the winter there.
Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way soon, and let them lack nothing.
Let our people also learn to lead in good work, for the sake of necessary needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
